attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'Paved with' is fairly read as 'enabled'. The universal 'every' is kept, and including AI matches the examples he lists next to it.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It does not require journalism to be the only cause. A universal claim needs evidence for each bubble or one clear in-scope counterexample, so that bar is fair. Leaving 19th-century booms as context is a reasonable choice, given his modern examples.

evidence.note: Peer-reviewed study of the 1840s Railway Mania. It found media sentiment did not inflate the bubble. Under the contract, historical booms are context only, and the study does not test deference in modern tech bubbles.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no list of tech bubbles and no causal evidence for the modern episodes (AI, crypto, metaverse, Clubhouse). The only item is a railway-era study, which the contract treats as context and not as a counterexample. The evidence neither establishes nor refutes the universal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the checkable core: a meagre return on massive capital from forced adoption. Leaving out the rhetorical 'reckoning' and 'revulsion' parts is acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading (realised benefits small relative to capital) is ordinary and sets no numeric cutoff. Using Q1 2025 for an ongoing claim is a reasonable choice by the drafter.

evidence.note: McKinsey survey from 2024. Over 80% report no tangible enterprise-level EBIT impact, but business units report cost cuts. Wrong period, and it does not compare benefits against capital.
$33.9B of private generative-AI funding in 2024. This is funding, not capex or returns, and it covers a different period.

reviews.rationale: Both items are from 2024. One measures self-reported impact and the other measures funding. Neither matches benefits to invested capital for the target quarter. Weak enterprise-level impact sits alongside reported business-unit savings, so the comparison the contract requires is not established either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The compound claim keeps all its parts: the loss, the 420% growth, the capex funding shortfall, and 'doesn't matter because' growth. The 'last quarter' is correctly Q1 2025.

contract.note: Reading the loss as net loss and growth as year-over-year quarterly revenue is ordinary. Counting available financing as 'money' is fair. Reading 'doesn't matter' as investor disregard is a reasonable plain reading.

evidence.note: Company earnings call: Q1 net loss of $315M, which is over $300M. The contract names company filings as the source for financial figures.
CNBC: Q1 revenue up 420% year over year, plus a $314.6M net loss. This confirms the growth figure.
Shares fell 5–7% after hours following the report. One price move with an unclear cause neither proves nor disproves investor disregard.
Company announcement: revolving credit expanded to $1.5B before the post. This undercuts a cash-only test but does not show all capex was funded.

reviews.rationale: The loss (over $300M) and the 420% growth hold. Nothing in the packet settles the funding-shortfall clause, because there is no matched schedule of cash, financing and capex payments. The investor-disregard mechanism is not established either. No part is contradicted, so under the contract the compound claim stays open.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The statement explains the AI boom through a system, but mixes in moral words ('rapacious') and undefined terms. The normalisation is faithful.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to narrow the claim to a testable substitute. No measure, threshold or counterfactual is given.

reviews.rationale: This is a broad systemic and moral characterisation. It has no defined outcome, causal threshold or comparison, so no evidence could fairly support or contradict it as written. The case is not broken; it simply cannot be scored.
